headlines.title_en: US pending home sales fall to lowest level since start of year
headlines.summary_en: US pending home sales for existing homes fell to their lowest level since the start of the year in July, reflecting a housing market weighed down by elevated mortgage rates and high prices. Data from the National Association of Realtors (NAR) showed the contract signing index dropped 2.3% to 71.2, the lowest since January and tied for the second-worst reading in data going back to 2001; economists polled had expected no change. Demand fell across all four major U.S. regions in the month. In the South, the nation's largest home-selling region, the pending sales index fell 2.2% to its lowest level since January 2025. Pending sales in the West fell 4.7%.

headlines.title_en: China has included 72 products, including building doors and windows, in the green building materials certification scope
headlines.summary_en: Reporters learned today that the State Administration for Market Regulation, together with the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, is gradually bringing 72 products in 6 major categories—including building doors and windows, ready-mixed concrete, and stone—into the green building materials certification scope, implementing full life-cycle quality control covering raw material extraction, production and manufacturing, use and distribution, and recycling and disposal, to build a solid quality and safety defense line for building materials from the source and enhance the green, low-carbon attributes of products. As of the end of June 2026, 5,725 enterprises nationwide had obtained green building materials certification, with 11,094 valid certificates, driving national green building materials revenue to nearly 130 billion yuan, up more than 10% year on year; it is expected that by the end of 2026, national green building materials revenue will exceed 300 billion yuan, with steady improvement in industry development quality and efficiency. (CCTV)

headlines.title_en: US July housing starts decline across the board, single-family starts fall to lowest since 2022
headlines.summary_en: U.S. housing starts fell in July, with single-family starts dropping to the lowest level since 2022. Data released by the U.S. government on Tuesday showed housing starts fell 12.4% in July to an annualized rate of 1.24 million units, below the expected 1.35 million. Single-family starts fell 9.9% to an annualized rate of 808,000 units, the lowest since November 2022. Multi-family starts fell nearly 17%, retreating after a sharp gain the prior month. The decline in housing starts shows the U.S. housing market remains sluggish. Since the start of the Iran conflict, rising mortgage rates and still-high home prices have continued to dampen housing demand.
